title: GLP-1 WEIGHT LOSS
subtitle: What you should know before choosing a GLP-1 weight loss program

sections.headline: Learn the Keys to Quality Care

elements.text: GLP-1 medications have changed the conversation around medical weight management.

For eligible patients, medications such as semaglutide and tirzepatide can be useful tools as part of a medically supervised weight-management plan. But deciding whether to pursue GLP-1 treatment involves more than choosing a medication or comparing prices.

The program you choose matters. An informed patient should understand who reviews their health information, how treatment is selected, whether appropriate monitoring or lab testing is offered, what support is provided, and what the program actually costs.

That’s why we created this guide. It isn’t intended to tell you whether you should take a GLP-1 medication. Only an appropriately licensed healthcare provider who evaluates your individual circumstances can make that determination.
Instead, this guide will help you understand the treatment category, recognize the elements of responsible care, and know what to consider before choosing a program.
Don’t choose a GLP-1 program based on the medication or price alone. Understand the care surrounding it.
Healthcare is more than medication. GLP-1 patients deserve continued support.
GLP-1 stands for glucagon-like peptide-1, a hormone produced naturally by the body.

Medications that act on the GLP-1 pathway can affect appetite, digestion and blood-sugar regulation. Among other effects, GLP-1 receptor agonists can help people feel fuller after eating and may slow the rate at which food leaves the stomach. When clinically appropriate, these effects can support weight management.
Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist. Tirzepatide works somewhat differently because it acts on both GLP-1 and GIP receptors.

Medication does not make nutrition, physical activity, sleep and other healthy habits irrelevant. Weight-management medications are generally intended to accompany lifestyle changes rather than replace them.
GLP-1 treatment can be an important part of weight management for many patients. But it is still medical treatment, not just a product purchase.
For eligible patients, WellPeps provides review by medical providers and continued support, with lab tests offered as needed.

sections.headline: Is GLP-1 Treatment Right for You?

elements.text: A GLP-1 weight loss program should begin with a medical question:
Is this treatment appropriate for this specific patient?

Not everyone who wants to lose weight is an appropriate candidate for every weight-management medication. A healthcare provider may consider factors such as health history, current medications, treatment goals, previous treatment experience and other individual circumstances.
That’s why an online health assessment shouldn’t simply be viewed as paperwork standing between you and a prescription. It is part of the clinical evaluation.
Submitting an assessment should not guarantee that medication will be prescribed. A licensed healthcare provider should determine whether treatment is medically appropriate.

In just a few minutes, a patient can fill out a private online health assessment for review by a licensed healthcare provider who may follow up with additional questions, as needed. In a few states, a video consult may also be required.
Will a licensed healthcare provider review my health information before treatment is prescribed?
Each patient’s unique health status and history is reviewed by a licensed healthcare provider to determine if a GLP-1 weight loss program is appropriate for the patient.
People considering GLP-1 treatment do not all have the same medical history, goals, preferences or treatment experience.

Responsible care recognizes those differences. The appropriate medication, formulation and treatment approach should be determined through a clinical process rather than treated as a one-size-fits-all purchase.
Patient preferences can be part of that discussion, but prescription and treatment decisions ultimately belong with the licensed healthcare provider overseeing the care.
Personalized care means your unique individual health information, goals, and preferences play a role in the healthcare provider’s treatment plan.
Begin with a health assessment and licensed-provider review. Treatment, if prescribed, is based on the patient’s individual information and the provider’s clinical judgment.

sections.headline: Semaglutide, Tirzepatide and Your Treatment Options

elements.text: Spend a few minutes researching weight-loss treatment online and you’ll encounter a confusing collection of names. They aren’t interchangeable terms.

items.title: SEMAGLUTIDE
items.desc: Acts primarily on the GLP-1 receptor.

items.title: TIRZEPATIDE
items.desc: Acts on both GIP and GLP-1 receptors.

items.title: ORAL OPTIONS
items.desc: May appeal to patients who prefer to avoid injections.

elements.text: Although the medications have similarities, their mechanisms aren’t identical, and there is no universally correct choice for every patient. Medical history, current medications, treatment goals, treatment experience, tolerability and other clinical factors may affect a provider’s recommendation. Delivery method can matter too.
Does the program offer provider-guided treatment options that take my individual health needs and preferences into account?

Every patient is unique. The medical provider will evaluate each patient, considering factors such as health history, body mass index, weight goals, current medications, and lab results, when recommending medication type, dosage and other aspects of the treatment plan.

sections.headline: When Might a Customized Formulation Be Considered?

elements.text: FDA-approved medications are generally the first consideration for GLP-1 treatment. But medicine isn’t always one-size-fits-all.

In certain circumstances, a licensed healthcare provider may determine that an individual patient’s medical needs are better addressed by a customized compounded formulation or dosage that differs from a commercially available medication.

Depending on the patient’s individual needs and the options available through the dispensing pharmacy, a medical provider may prescribe compounded semaglutide or tirzepatide formulations that incorporate ingredients such as:

items.title: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)
items.desc: An essential vitamin involved in metabolism, nervous-system function and the body’s use of nutrients.

items.title: Vitamin B12 (Cyanocobalamin)
items.desc: An essential vitamin involved in red blood cell formation, nerve function and cellular energy metabolism.

items.title: L-Carnitine (Levocarnitine)
items.desc: A naturally occurring substance involved in transporting fatty acids into cells where they can be used in energy production.

items.title: Glycine
items.desc: An amino acid used by the body in protein production and a variety of metabolic processes.

items.title: Niacinamide (Vitamin B3)
items.desc: A form of vitamin B3 involved in cellular energy metabolism and normal cellular function.

elements.text: A licensed provider may determine that a customized formulation is appropriate based on an individual patient’s medical needs. The presence of an additional ingredient does not mean that the formulation is more effective for weight loss than FDA-approved semaglutide or tirzepatide.

The decision to prescribe a compounded formulation should be based on an individual medical evaluation and a specific patient need—not simply on price or preference. Unlike commercially available FDA-approved medications, customized compounded medications are prepared for individual patients based on a provider’s prescription.
Is my treatment simply a standard medication offered to everyone—or has a licensed provider considered whether the formulation is appropriate for my individual needs?

Treatment begins with a medical review. When appropriate, a licensed provider determines the medication, formulation and dosing approach based on the patient’s individual health information and treatment needs.
The names on a program’s menu tell you less than you might think. Here is what actually separates the options.

items.title: SEMAGLUTIDE
items.desc: GLP-1 receptor agonist. FDA-approved brands: Wegovy (weight management), Ozempic (type 2 diabetes). Weekly injection; a tablet form also exists.

items.title: TIRZEPATIDE
items.desc: Acts on GIP and GLP-1 receptors. FDA-approved brands: Zepbound (weight management), Mounjaro (type 2 diabetes). Weekly injection.

items.title: INJECTION
items.desc: One weekly dose from a small pen. Most weight-management evidence comes from injectable forms.

items.title: ORAL TABLET
items.desc: A daily tablet for patients who prefer to avoid needles. Timing and food rules matter more.

elements.text: “FDA-approved” means that specific product was reviewed by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for safety and effectiveness. Compounded semaglutide or tirzepatide is prepared by a licensed pharmacy for an individual patient and is not itself FDA-approved, so the pharmacy’s licensing and sourcing matter. Newer molecules such as retatrutide are investigational and not approved outside clinical trials.
Which medication and form are you recommending for me, and is it FDA-approved or compounded?
WellPeps providers discuss medication type, delivery form and approval status with each patient. Prescriptions are filled only through licensed U.S.-based pharmacies.

sections.headline: Why Lab Tests and Monitoring Matter

elements.text: The scale tells you one thing. It doesn’t tell you everything about your health.

Medical weight management should take place in the context of your overall health—not simply the number of pounds lost. Depending on an individual patient’s circumstances, a healthcare provider may consider medical history, symptoms, treatment response and laboratory information as part of care.
If a GLP-1 program does not offer lab testing as part of treatment, you should ask why.

items.title: SYMPTOMS

items.title: LABS

elements.text: That does not mean every GLP-1 patient requires the same laboratory panel at the same interval. Testing should be clinically appropriate and determined by healthcare professionals. What matters is whether a program can support appropriate monitoring when it is needed.
Ask whether lab testing is offered as part of the program.

sections.headline: Side Effects Are Part of the Conversation

elements.text: Every prescription medication has potential risks and side effects.

With GLP-1 therapies, commonly reported side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal discomfort and decreased appetite. Gastrointestinal symptoms may be more noticeable when treatment begins or following dose increases and may improve over time for some patients.

items.title: KNOW
items.desc: Understand common effects

items.title: WATCH
items.desc: Pay attention to persistent or worsening symptoms

items.title: CONTACT
items.desc: Seek appropriate clinical guidance when needed

elements.text: Patients should follow the instructions provided with their medication and contact an appropriate healthcare professional about persistent, worsening or concerning symptoms. Potentially serious symptoms may require urgent or emergency medical evaluation.
Patients should not independently stop, restart or change prescribed medication without appropriate clinical guidance.
Ask if the provider offers continued support and lab follow-up tests if needed, as part of their treatment plan.

GLP-1 patients on WellPeps plans receive continued support, with lab tests offered as needed. Additionally, patients can discuss any side effects with medical providers, plus discuss adjusting dosage or other treatment options.

sections.headline: Your care shouldn’t end when your medication ships.

elements.text: It’s easy for telehealth weight management to look like an e-commerce transaction: complete a form, receive a prescription if appropriate, and receive a package. But healthcare shouldn’t stop at the shipping confirmation. Weight-management treatment can evolve over time. Patients can have questions, experience side effects, encounter plateaus or need additional support.

sections.headline: Medication Quality and U.S. Fulfillment Matter

elements.text: Prescription weight-management treatment should take place through legitimate healthcare and pharmacy channels.
Patients should receive medication only when prescribed by an appropriately licensed healthcare provider and should have access to the information and instructions that accompany their prescription.

For consumers comparing online programs, the broader point is straightforward: medication sourcing and fulfillment should be part of a responsible healthcare process, not an anonymous online transaction.

Patients should understand where their medication is prepared and dispensed. When comparing programs, ask whether prescription medications are formulated and fulfilled through appropriately licensed U.S.-based pharmacies.
Ask if your medication will be formulated by licensed U.S. pharmacies.

elements.text: Two programs advertising a similar monthly price may not include the same things.

Before comparing costs, find out what you’re actually paying for. Depending on the program, charges may involve medication, provider evaluation, ongoing support, laboratory services, shipping, coaching, membership or platform fees, and cancellation terms.
Unfortunately, some telehealth companies advertise low prices, but then charge patients extra for additional services, or don’t offer important services at all.
